name: Push Plastic
summary: US filament extruder established September 2013, running its own production since inception and claiming 25+ years of plastics experience behind it. Unusually broad engineering catalog for a small US operation — PEI, PMMA and PC+PBT alongside the commodity materials — in both 1.75 mm and 2.85 mm, with SAM.gov certification for government and institutional sales.

product_lines.name: High Heat + Tough PLA (HH+T PLA - 3D870)
product_lines.notes: Built on NatureWorks Ingeo 3D870, the fast-crystallising annealable high-heat PLA resin (same family as Fusion HT-PLA and Protopasta HTPLA). No dedicated high-heat-PLA id exists; not mapped to pla-plus because the toughness claim comes from the resin grade rather than a documented impact modifier.

product_lines.name: ABS / Matte ABS
product_lines.notes: Standard ABS plus a matte-finish variant.

product_lines.name: PC+PBT
product_lines.notes: Polycarbonate/PBT engineering blend; TDS gives specific gravity 1.18 (ASTM D792) and tensile yield ~15,000 psi (ASTM D638).

product_lines.name: Carbon Fiber PC+PBT
product_lines.notes: Carbon-fibre-reinforced PC/PBT blend. Listed against pc-pbt for family context only — no pc-pbt-cf id exists.

product_lines.name: Nylon
product_lines.notes: Unfilled nylon; exact PA type not confirmed in public copy, so pa6/pa12 are not asserted.

product_lines.name: Carbon Fiber Nylon
product_lines.notes: Sold as 'Carbon Fiber Nylon Filament' — PA + carbon fibre, not PLA-CF or PETG-CF. PA type unconfirmed and no generic pa-cf id exists, so pa is listed for family context only.

product_lines.name: PMMA (Acrylic)
product_lines.notes: True poly(methyl methacrylate) — a distinct polymer family with no id in this catalog; not a PETG or PLA rebrand.

product_lines.name: PEI 1010
product_lines.notes: Unfilled polyetherimide on ULTEM 1010 chemistry, the standard ultra-high-temp PEI grade.

product_lines.name: TPU
product_lines.notes: True TPU; shore hardness not confirmed on the pages reviewed, so no durometer-specific id is assigned.

product_lines.name: HIPS
product_lines.notes: High-impact polystyrene, typically used as a sacrificial support for ABS.

product_lines.name: Soluble Support
product_lines.notes: Separate solvent/water-soluble support line; base chemistry (PVA vs BVOH vs HIPS) not confirmed on the pages reviewed.

additional_notes: Location: Springdale, Arkansas. Primary source is Push Plastic's own Terms of Service (Sec. 18: '605 Bain Street Suite #B, Springdale, US 72764'; ZIP 72764 is Arkansas, state not printed), corroborated by the 3printr manufacturer listing and an Advanced Manufacturing article on Arkansas 3D printing. This supersedes the earlier 'Little Rock, Arkansas' from Filament Cheat Sheet (secondary). In-house US extrusion since September 2013 (factory tour video; 'USA-made' per retailer) with a 100% virgin material claim (no regrind). Relationship re-check 2026-11-06: no OEM, white-label or parent relationship found in either direction, so oem_relationships stays empty; the rumoured Filastruder connection remains uncorroborated (zero hits connecting them). SAM.gov certified, CAGE Code 8CH52. Also offers CF PETG and CF ABS, spools up to 25 kg, bulk, pellets and custom colour matching, and resells 3D printers, accessories and resin/color pellets; sold direct (Shopify) plus Amazon and top3dshop. SpoolmanDB PR #438 (open, migrated from Open Filament Database) adds 15 filaments / 79 colours. Typical PLA/ABS pricing $22-32/kg; Filament Cheat Sheet rates the brand Tier B.

provenance.conflicts: Resolved 2026-11-06: the Terms of Service address '605 Bain Street Suite #B Springdale US 72764' was read directly on pushplastic.com (state inferred from ZIP; corroborated by 3printr and Advanced Manufacturing), superseding Filament Cheat Sheet's 'Little Rock'. A Birdeye directory lists a second Springdale address (1206 Esi Dr, 72764), unverified. Arkansas Secretary of State (POST-only search form) and SAM.gov (JS shell) could not be read, so the registered entity name and CAGE 8CH52 are unconfirmed. 'No relationships' is medium confidence (absence of evidence). Carbon-fiber base polymers are inferred.
